title: Part Three: Darby and the System Crossing the Atlantic

sections.brief: John Nelson Darby (1800-1882): law, Church of Ireland curacy, Dublin meeting and Plymouth Brethren, 1848 split; Powerscourt conferences 1831-33 (Fazio on the 1831 notebooks); the Margaret MacDonald / Irving origin claim (Tregelles, MacPherson 1973) against Darby's 1827 account, Strand 1975 review, Ice; Hodge on the new rapture. Figures: compare; time

What dispensationalism teaches in plain terms: two peoples/two plans (Darby, Geneva 1840), Daniel's paused clock, any-moment rapture then Israel's seventieth week; tests the claim that Darby made a Jewish return a precondition (corrects B1 and rd1 s05); Gaebelein 1905 on Zionism as unbelief. Figures: flow; compare

Darby's North American journeys (at least five, 1862-77; eschatology adopted, ecclesiology not); Brookes and the Niagara conferences (1868/1875/1876 origins, Niagara-on-the-Lake 1883-97, 1878 creed Art. XIV 'Israel shall be restored'); 1878 New York prophetic conference; Moody, MBI 1886 and the Bible institutes; Scofield's apprenticeship; Gaebelein; corrects 'non-existent before 1909'. Figures: time; compare
